Consider a sequence of normal irreducible globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds X0 99K X1 99K X2 99K · · · . On Xi, let Bi be the strict transform of B0, let Mi = MXi be the trace of the same b-divisor, and assume that Di = KXi + Bi + Mi is Q-Cartier. Transport the canonical representatives under the induced identifications of prime divisors. Suppose that every step is given by a diagram (1.2) Xi Zi Xi+1 fi f+ i GENERALIZED LOG CANONICAL FLIPS ON KÄHLER FOURFOLDS 3 where Zi is normal compact Kähler, both maps are projective small bimeromorphic morphisms with connected fibers, neither is an isomorphism, and −Di is fi-ample, Di+1 is f+ i -ample. Here small means that the exceptional locus contains no prime divisor. Then the sequence is finite.

candidates.statement: Let (T, B+M) be gklt rational generalized data on a normal compact Kähler space, with effective boundary of finite support and an absolutely nef rational datum carried by a projective modification. There is ε > 0 such that every global place satisfies a(E; T, B + M) ≥ ε, 6 OPENAI and only finitely many places exceptional over T satisfy a(E; T, B + M) < 1 + ε. No Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity is assumed. (i) Every negative extremal ray at every stage has the contraction and, when birational, a positive model required by Definition 1.1. (ii) Every program of Definition 1.1 starting from (X, B) has finitely many birational steps, for every sequence of permitted choices. (iii) Every maximal program ends either at a projective lc pair with nef adjoint, or at a Mori fibre space: a projective contraction with connected fibres, relative Picard number one, lower- dimensional normal base, and relatively ample negative adjoint. An already nef input has a zero-step completed program.

candidates.label: Corollary 2.2
candidates.heading: Corollary 2.2.
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.1, lc and klt are preserved. For a small step, an effective terminal pair remains terminal. At a divisor-losing step the discrepancy of every lost prime divisor increases strictly.

candidates.label: Corollary 2.4
candidates.heading: Corollary 2.4.
candidates.statement: To prove termination of a fourfold program it suffices to show that, on its small tail, positive-side bad surfaces occur only finitely often.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.4.

Consecutive junctions can be joined by: (i) decreasing the coefficient of each Ei,s to 1 − ai+1(s) on Yi; (ii) a finite sequence, possibly empty, of small negative terminal flips over Zi. Every labeled prime persists through the chain. All coefficients are nonincreasing, and the discrepancy of every valuation is nondecreasing, including across coefficient changes.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.6
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.6.
candidates.statement: After truncating the small downstairs tail, every surface contained in either bad locus of every remaining step has generic-point mld greater than one and is generically in the smooth locus of its ambient model. At each remaining crepant junction, every varying label has downstairs center of codimension at least three. Consequently the reduced union of varying labels is mapped by pi to a set of dimension at most one.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.2.
candidates.statement: On the prepared terminal chain, the integer D(Y, Θ) has the following properties. (i) It is nonnegative at every crepant junction. candidates.heading: Theorem 7.4.
candidates.statement: Every program in Definition 1.1 starting with a projective klt fourfold pair over C with rational boundary has finitely many birational steps. No pseudo-effectivity hypothesis is needed.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.5
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.5.
candidates.statement: Let (X, B) be a projective lc fourfold pair over C with rational boundary, with D = KX + B Q-Cartier. If this contraction is birational, it has an output in the precise convention of Definition 1.1: the positive map is small, possibly an isomorphism, and its actual adjoint with the strict boundary is relatively ample and lc. candidates.label: Proposition 9.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.2.
candidates.statement: Let k be any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A countable program of the kind in Definition 1.1, including all its prescribed ray choices, descends to a common countable algebraically closed subfield of k. After embedding that subfield in C, it gives a program with the same step types and relative signs, the same boundary coefficients, and the same singularity properties. In particular an infinite birational program over k would give an infinite birational program over C.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Termination of ordinary programs
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Termination of ordinary programs).
candidates.statement: Let X be a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold, with a canonical Weil divisor KX, and let ∆ ≥ 0 be a rational divisor such that (X, ∆) is klt. Then every maximal ordinary negative-ray program starting on (X, ∆) terminates. Its birational steps form a finite sequence (X, ∆) = (X0, ∆0) 99K · · · 99K (Xn, ∆n). Every Xi is normal, compact Kähler and globally Weil Q-factorial; every (Xi, ∆i) is klt, and Di = KXi + ∆i is Q-Cartier. The canonical divisors are the transforms of the specified datum. The following alternatives hold. (i) If D = KX + ∆ is pseudo-effective, then Dn is nef. The composite ϕ : X 99K Xn extracts no prime divisor, and a(E; X, ∆) ≤ a(E; Xn, ∆n) for every prime divisor over the two models, with strict inequality for every prime on X contracted by ϕ. MINIMAL MODEL PROGRAMS ON KÄHLER FOURFOLDS 3 (ii) If D is not pseudo-effective, there is a projective surjective morphism g : Xn → S with connected fibres, where S is normal compact Kähler, dim S < 4, ρ(Xn/S) = 1, and −Dn is g-ample. For each negative contraction, including g, the relative Bott–Chern dimension is one. If X is globally strongly Q-factorial, so is every Xi. The same conclusions hold in the intrinsic formulation with the canonical rational line bundle in place of a chosen canonical Weil divisor. In either formulation the first model is exactly X.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.24
candidates.name: Finite ordinary programs
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.24 (Finite ordinary programs).
candidates.statement: Let (X, B) be a rational klt pair on a normal globally Weil Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold. The canonical datum may be a specified canonical Weil divisor or the intrinsic canonical rational line bundle. Then every maximal ordinary negative-ray program starts on X and terminates. All models remain normal, compact Kähler, globally Weil Q-factorial and klt; global strong Q-factoriality is preserved when imposed initially. Every negative contraction is projective, with relative line-bundle rank and relative Bott–Chern dimension one. If KX + B is pseudo-effective, the endpoint has nef adjoint. The composite extracts no divisor, discrepancies do not decrease, and strictly increase for every prime on X that is contracted. If KX + B is not pseudo-effective, the endpoint has a projective Mori fibre contraction to a normal compact Kähler space of smaller dimension, with connected fibres and relatively antiample adjoint. In particular, these conclusions imply Theorem 1.2.

The construction is available after every finite prefix whose final adjoint is not curve-nef over V . For gklt data one may choose any negative extremal ray in the global degree cone.

candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of condition (i) of Theorem 1.1 and the boundary construction of Theorem 4.7, there are a contractible Stein manifold M, biholomorphic to the boundedly realizable tower P, an equivariant surjective submersion f : V → M, and an 44 equivariant holomorphic map fX : e X → M with f = fXµ. Both maps have connected fibres. Their fibres have simultaneous projective compactifications with analytic holes locally on M, after a deck translation. The normal-source fibres are normal and semialgebraically compactifiable up to biholomorphism, and fX is flat. Suppose additionally that the image Λ of the deck action on M is discrete and acts freely. Then the descended proper map X → M/Λ, its pullback to M, and every connected finite covering family of that pullback are flat and topologically locally trivial, with connected normal projective fibres. Their induced resolution families are smooth proper projective families; the resolution maps are proper, have connected point fibres, and are bimeromorphic on every fibre. The induced maps on integral degree-one cohomology are morphisms of local systems.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.4
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.4.
candidates.statement: The image Λ is discrete in Aut(M) and acts cocompactly on M.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.6
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.6.
candidates.statement: Under the intrinsic-projection hypotheses recalled above, the transverse image is discrete and cocompact. After a finite cover it acts freely, and M is biholomorphic to a bounded symmetric domain, with a point allowed.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.8
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.8.
candidates.statement: After the finite-cover replacement of Lemma 6.5, let K = ker(Γ → Λ). The group K is finitely generated and virtually abelian. For each m ∈ M, it acts on f−1(m) as the deck group of a connected regular covering of a smooth projective fibre.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.3
candidates.name: The proper map to the affine base
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.3 (The proper map to the affine base).
candidates.statement: There is a Γ-equivariant proper flat surjection j : U −→ T, T ≃ M × Ca , whose fibres are connected, simply connected, normal projective varieties. The action of Γ on T is proper and cocompact and has finite stabilizers. A polarization of the finite cover of X pulls back to a Γ-invariant line bundle L on U, ample on each fibre of j.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.7
candidates.name: Triviality of the compact factor
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.7 (Triviality of the compact factor).
candidates.statement: There is a simply connected normal projective variety F such that e X ≃ M × Ca × F.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.8
candidates.name: The converse
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.8 (The converse).
candidates.statement: If e X ≃ D × Cm × F, with D a bounded symmetric domain and F projective, then e X is biholomorphic to a semialgebraic open subset of a projective variety.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.1
candidates.name: Remmert reduction of semialgebraic covers
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.1 (Remmert reduction of semialgebraic covers).
candidates.statement: Let X be a connected normal projective complex variety whose ordinary universal cover U has a semialgebraic projective-open presentation. Write U ≃ B×F, where B = D×Cm, as in Theorem 1.1. Then U is holomorphically convex and the projection p : U → B is its Remmert reduction: B is Stein, p is proper with connected compact normal projective fibres, and the canonical map OB → p∗OU is an isomorphism. Moreover, U is Stein if and only if F is a point.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.2
candidates.name: Singer vanishing for semialgebraic covers
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.2 (Singer vanishing for semialgebraic covers).
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth connected closed aspherical projective complex n-fold whose ordinary universal cover has a semialgebraic projective- open presentation. Its L2-Betti numbers, computed from the reduced L2-cohomology of the universal cover, satisfy b (2) j (X) = 0 (j ≥ 0, j ̸= n). If m > 0 for the affine factor in the product constructed in the proof of Theorem 1.1, then b (2) j (X) = 0 for every j ≥ 0.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.1
candidates.name: Quasi-projective covers
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.1 (Quasi-projective covers).
candidates.statement: Let X be a connected normal projective variety over C, with ordinary universal cover U. The following are equivalent: (i) U is biholomorphic to a quasi-projective variety. (ii) There are a finite étale Galois cover X′ → X, an abelian variety A, and a morphism α : X′ → A that is a locally trivial holomorphic fibre bundle with simply connected projective fibre. (iii) For some integer m ≥ 0 and some simply connected projective variety F, there is a biholo- morphism U ≃ Cm × F. A point is allowed as the abelian variety or the fibre. More generally, let V → X be a connected infinite étale Galois covering of complex spaces, with V biholomorphic to a quasi-projective variety. There are an intermediate finite étale Galois cover X′ → X, a morphism α : X′ → A to an abelian variety that is a locally trivial holomorphic fibre bundle, and an étale cover e A → A, where e A has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety, such that V → X′ is biholomorphic as a covering to X′ ×A e A −→ X′ . No algebraicity of the deck transformations is assumed.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.2
candidates.name: Projective affine-space uniformization
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.2 (Projective affine-space uniformization).
candidates.statement: Let X be a connected smooth projective complex n-fold, where n ≥ 0. If its ordinary universal cover is biholomorphic to Cn, then there is a finite étale Galois cover A → X with A an abelian variety.

manuscripts.title: Symmetry of semialgebraic bounded domains with compact quotient

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let U be a nonempty connected semialgebraic bounded open subset of a complex affine variety. Suppose that a group Γ of biholomorphisms acts properly discontinuously on U and that U/Γ is compact. Then U is smooth and is biholomorphic to a bounded symmetric domain.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.2.
candidates.statement: If U is not a point, then it is a complex manifold of positive dimension and lies in the smooth locus of a single irreducible component V of the ambient variety.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.3
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.3.
candidates.statement: The function dU is a finite distance inducing the usual topology of U. Every closed dU -ball is compact.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: Generic boundary data
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (Generic boundary data).
candidates.statement: In the coordinates of Equation (3.2), almost every s∗ ∈ B has the following two properties. (i) There are a neighborhood B∗ ⊂ B of s∗, a number ε > 0, and a real-analytic map ψ : B∗ × (−ε, ε) → Rk such that ψ(s, 0) = 0, ψ(s, u) ∈ As (s ∈ B∗, 0 < u < ε). (ii) Set E(s, t) = Rk \ t−1 As, d(s, t; v) = min{1, dist(v, E(s, t))}. 9 There is a 1-Lipschitz function d∗ : Rk → [0, 1] such that, for every compact L ⊂ Rk, lim s→s∗ t↓0 sup v∈L |d(s, t; v) − d∗(v)| = 0. (3.4) The set F = {v : d∗(v) = 0} is a closed cone, invariant under every positive real dilation, and 0 ∈ F. In particular, for every sequence sj → s∗, tj ↓ 0, and vj → v, one has d(sj, tj; vj) → d∗(v). If v ∈ F, then dist(vj, E(sj, tj)) −→ 0. If v / ∈ F, some fixed ball about v is contained in t−1 j Asj for all sufficiently large j.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.4
candidates.name: A good supported point
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.4 (A good supported point).
candidates.statement: There are a boundary cell S in the first alternative of Lemma 3.1, a good point p ∈ S, and k = 2n − dimR S entire functions h1, . . . , hk on CN such that hj(p) = 1, |hj(q)| ≤ exp(−|q − p|2 ) (q ∈ U), 1 ≤ j ≤ k. (3.5) The real covectors d log |hj||TpV are linearly independent and annihilate TpS. Consequently, in coordinates (z, w) ∈ Cn−k × Ck centered at p with TpS = {Im w = 0}, their holomorphic logarithmic differentials have the form d log hj(p) = iβj dw, where the βj are linearly independent real rows.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.2
candidates.name: Noncollapse
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2 (Noncollapse).
candidates.statement: At the point selected in Proposition 3.4, the excluded cone in Proposition 3.3 satisfies F ̸= Rk.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Two-sided convergence of the scaled sets
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Two-sided convergence of the scaled sets).
candidates.statement: There are an invertible real linear map L : Rk → Rk and a vector Q of real quadratic forms on Cm such that, with R(Z, W) = L(Im W) − Q(Z), O = {(Z, W) : R(Z, W) / ∈ F}, the following hold. (i) Every compact subset of O is contained in Dt for all sufficiently small t > 0. (ii) For every ξ ∈ Cn with R(ξ) ∈ F and every sequence tj ↓ 0, there are ξj / ∈ Dtj such that ξj → ξ. These excluded points can be chosen within the scaled coordinate charts.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.2
candidates.name: Quadratic model
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.2 (Quadratic model).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, with n ≥ 1, there are integers 1 ≤ k ≤ n, m = n − k, a nonempty connected open cone C ⊂ Rk, and a vector H of Hermitian forms on Cm such that U is biholomorphic to D = {(z, w) ∈ Cm × Ck : Im w − H(z, z) ∈ C}. (5.3) Here C is invariant under every positive dilation, and H is complex linear in its first argument. There are independent real linear functionals ℓ1, . . . , ℓk on Rk and a constant c > 0 such that ℓa(y) > 0 (y ∈ C), ℓa(H(z, z)) ≥ c∥z∥2 (z ∈ Cm ), 1 ≤ a ≤ k. (5.4) The original action transfers to a properly discontinuous action on D with compact quotient. No freeness assumption is required.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: Vey
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (Vey).
candidates.statement: Let D ⊂ Cm × Ck be a connected domain biholomorphic to a bounded domain. Suppose that D contains a point (0, w) and is invariant under (z, w) 7−→ (z, w + a), (z, w) 7−→ (eiθ z, w), (z, w) 7−→ (r1/2 z, rw) for every a ∈ Rk, θ ∈ R, and r > 0. If D is divisible, it is biholomorphic to a bounded symmetric domain. The case m = 0 is included.

manuscripts.title: Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There is a finite integer N > 3, divisible by eight, and there are reduced polynomials f1, f2 ∈ R[z1, . . . , zN ], weighted homogeneous for positive rational weights, such that: (i) each fj has an isolated critical point at the origin; 1 (ii) ord0 f1 = 2 and ord0 f2 = 3; (iii) there is a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (CN , V (f1), 0) ∼ = (CN , V (f2), 0).

candidates.label: Theorem 2.1
candidates.name: Milnor
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Milnor).
candidates.statement: Let s ≥ 2, and let f : (Cs, 0) → (C, 0) be a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point at 0, with f(0) = 0. For sufficiently small ε > 0, the link Kf = f−1(0) ∩ S2s−1 ε is a smooth closed manifold of dimension 2s − 3, and f/|f| : S2s−1 ε \ Kf −→ S1 is a locally trivial fibration. Each fiber is the interior of its closure Ff , a compact manifold with boundary Kf . Both Ff and its interior are homotopy equivalent to a finite bouquet of (s − 1)-spheres. The link is (s − 3)-connected.
candidates.cited_by: Theorem 2.1 (Milnor).

candidates.label: Theorem 2.2
candidates.name: Thom–Sebastiani–Sakamoto
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.2 (Thom–Sebastiani–Sakamoto).
candidates.statement: Suppose f and g have isolated critical points in a and b variables, respectively. There is an isomorphism of integral lattices Lf+g ∼ = Lf ⊗Z Lg under which Mf+g ∼ = Mf ⊗ Mg, Sf+g ∼ = (−1)ab Sf ⊗ Sg. The assertion includes one-variable powers, with reduced zeroth homology.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.3
candidates.name: Weighted homogeneous spectrum
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.3 (Weighted homogeneous spectrum).
candidates.statement: If f is weighted homogeneous of normalized degree 1 and has an isolated critical point, its spectral polynomial is Pf (t) = X β∈Sp+ (f) tβ = s Y j=1 twj − t 1 − twj . (2.2) Exponents are counted with multiplicity. Their classes modulo Z determine the eigenvalues of Mf by exponentiation, with a fixed choice of sign in the exponent. The operator Mf has finite order.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.4
candidates.name: Real Seifert forms from the spectrum
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.4 (Real Seifert forms from the spectrum).
candidates.statement: Let f and g be isolated weighted homogeneous singularities in the same number of variables. If their multisets of positive spectral exponents agree modulo 2Z, their real Seifert forms are isomorphic.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.5
candidates.name: Hertling–Mase
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.5 (Hertling–Mase).
candidates.statement: Suppose f is a sum of chains xa1 1 x2 + · · · + x ar−1 r−1 xr + xar r , ai ≥ 2, 6 including chains with r = 1. Write the characteristic polynomial of Mf as Q d Φd(t)cd , where Φd is cyclotomic. Then, as an integral module with operator t = Mf , (Lf , Mf ) ∼ = max cd M j=1 Z[t]/ pj(t)  , pj(t) = Y cd≥j Φd(t). (2.3) In particular, the eigenvalues with multiplicity determine this integral monodromy module within the indicated class of singularities.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.6
candidates.name: Hasse–Minkowski
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.6 (Hasse–Minkowski).
candidates.statement: Two nondegenerate quadratic forms over a number field F are isometric over F if and only if they are isometric over Fv for every place v, including the archimedean places.
candidates.cited_by: We use the number-field form of the theorem; see [16, Theorem 25.64(c) and the following discussion]; see also [20, Chapter VI].
references: [16] J. S. Milne. Algebraic Groups: The Theory of Group Schemes of Finite Type over a Field, volume 170 of Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, 2022. URL https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf. Corrected reprint of the 2017 edition.
[20] O. T. O’Meara. Introduction to Quadratic Forms, volume 117 of Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften. Springer-Verlag, Berlin–Göttingen–Heidelberg, 1963.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.7
candidates.name: Strong approximation
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.7 (Strong approximation).
candidates.statement: Let G be a connected, simply connected, absolutely almost simple algebraic group over a number field F. If Q v|∞ G(Fv) is noncompact, then G(F) is dense in G(AF,f ), the group of finite adelic points.
candidates.cited_by: Theorem 2.7 (Strong approximation).

candidates.label: Theorem 2.8
candidates.name: Smale and Levine
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.8 (Smale and Levine).
candidates.statement: A smooth closed manifold of dimension d ≥ 5 that is homotopy equivalent to Sd is homeomorphic to Sd. Let q ≥ 3, and let K1, K2 ⊂ S2q+1 be smooth oriented submanifolds homeomorphic to S2q−1. Suppose the knots are simple, meaning π1(S2q+1 \ Kj) ∼ = Z, πi(S2q+1 \ Kj) = 0 (2 ≤ i ≤ q − 1). If their integral Seifert matrices are congruent, then they are ambiently isotopic. In particular their embedded sphere pairs are homeomorphic.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3
candidates.name: The seeds
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.3 (The seeds).
candidates.statement: There are real-coefficient weighted homogeneous polynomials p1, p2, each in an even number s0 of variables, such that: 1. both are sums, in disjoint variables, of chains with exponents at least 2, and both have isolated critical points; 2. ord0 p1 = 2 and ord0 p2 = 3; 3. their spectral multisets are equal modulo 2; 4. their real Seifert forms are isomorphic, and, separately, their integral monodromy modules are isomorphic; 5. both monodromy operators have order dividing D = 312.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.4
candidates.name: Removing eigenvalue one
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.4 (Removing eigenvalue one).
candidates.statement: In two new variables on each side, put qj = pj + x5 + y7 , j = 1, 2, s = s0 + 2. (3.8) These are real-coefficient isolated sums of chains in the same even number s of variables, with orders 2 and 3. Their real Seifert forms are isomorphic, and their integral monodromy modules are isomorphic. Both monodromies have odd order dividing m = 312 · 5 · 7, and neither has eigenvalue 1.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Odd-prime tensor squares
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Odd-prime tensor squares).
candidates.statement: Let L be a finite free Zℓ-module, with ℓ odd, and let T be an automorphism of L. If B1, B2 are unimodular symmetric forms preserved by T, then (L ⊗ L, T ⊗ T, B1 ⊗ B1) ∼ = (L ⊗ L, T ⊗ T, B2 ⊗ B2) by an equivariant integral isometry.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.4
candidates.name: Dyadic uniqueness
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.4 (Dyadic uniqueness).
candidates.statement: Let L be a finite free Z2-module, and let T satisfy Tm = 1 for an odd m. Suppose 1 is not an eigenvalue of T on L ⊗ Q2. Any two T-invariant unimodular symmetric forms on L are equivariantly isometric over Z2.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.7
candidates.name: Local and rational square isometries
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.7 (Local and rational square isometries).
candidates.statement: Set Aj = (Lj, Tj, Bj)⊗2 . There are an equivariant rational isometry R : A1 ⊗ Q −→ A2 ⊗ Q and, for every prime ℓ, an equivariant isometry Dℓ : A1 ⊗ Zℓ −→ A2 ⊗ Zℓ. These can be chosen so that Dℓ = R after extension to Qℓ for all but finitely many primes.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.4
candidates.name: Integral equivariant isometry
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.4 (Integral equivariant isometry).
candidates.statement: The triples H1 and H2 in (5.5) are isometric over Z: there is a lattice isomorphism U : Λ1 −→ Λ2 satisfying UΘ1 = Θ2U, Ut β2U = β1.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.3
candidates.name: Negative answer to Arnold’s corank problem
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.3 (Negative answer to Arnold’s corank problem).
candidates.statement: In the finite ambient dimension N > 3 divisible by eight in (6.2), the polynomials f1, f2 in (6.1) have different Hessian coranks, although their reduced complex hypersurface germs are ambiently homeomorphic. Both polynomials have real coefficients, are weighted homogeneous with positive rational weights, and have isolated critical points at the origin.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.4
candidates.name: Right-topological multiplicity and parity counterexamples
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.4 (Right-topological multiplicity and parity counterexamples).
candidates.statement: For the same polynomials f1, f2 and the single finite ambient dimension N > 3 divisible by eight in Theorem 1.1, there is a homeomorphism germ φ : (CN , 0) −→ (CN , 0) such that f1 = f2 ◦ φ. Nevertheless, their multiplicities are respectively 2 and 3. Thus neither multiplicity nor multiplicity modulo two is invariant under topological right equivalence, even for reduced real-coefficient weighted homogeneous holomorphic germs with positive rational weights and isolated critical points at the origin.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.5
candidates.name: Initial-form Milnor-fibre counterexamples
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.5 (Initial-form Milnor-fibre counterexamples).
candidates.statement: In the single ambient dimension N + 1, put e fj(z, t) = fj(z) + t2 , j = 1, 2. The germs e f1, e f2 : (CN+1, 0) → (C, 0) are topologically right equivalent and have isolated critical points at the origin, but H0 ( e f1)−1 ∗ (1); Z  ∼ = Z, H0 ( e f2)−1 ∗ (1); Z  ∼ = Z2 . Thus integral homology of the initial-form Milnor fibre is not invariant under topological right equivalence, already in degree zero. In particular, the initial-form Milnor-fibre homotopy conjecture of Budur, Fernández de Bobadilla, Lê, and Nguyen [3, Conjecture 1.7 in arXiv v3] fails.

manuscripts.title: Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five

candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.

candidates.name: Analytic germs and their orders

After solving the smooth ambient equations in analytic local coordinates, f0,s has order five and f1,s has order four. Both are reduced convergent germs.

(4.1) The rational orthogonal filling form on these coordinates is −sd|K ⊥ (sh ⊗ e). (4.2) The lattice and form are those of a genuine local Milnor page of fs in the smooth ambient germ Cs.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.6
candidates.name: Integral Seifert congruence
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.6 (Integral Seifert congruence).
candidates.statement: For the two germs constructed above, the two integral Milnor Seifert forms (Λ0, s0) and (Λ1, s1) are isometric.

manuscripts.title: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Global Spherical Shell conjecture
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Global Spherical Shell conjecture).
candidates.statement: Let X be a connected compact complex surface with b1(X) = 1, b2(X) > 0, κ(X) = −∞. Assume that X is minimal: it contains no smooth rational curve of self-intersection −1. Then there are an open neighborhood U of S3 = {z ∈ C2 : |z| = 1} in C2 \ {0}, an open subset Σ ⊂ X, and a biholomorphism ϕ : U −→ Σ such that X \ Σ is connected.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Deformation and smooth topology
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Deformation and smooth topology).
candidates.statement: Let X satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, and put b = b2(X). There is a small one-parameter deformation X → ∆ over a disk about 0, with X0 ≃ X, such that every nonzero fiber is obtained from a primary Hopf surface by exactly b successive point blowups. The centers may be infinitely near. Moreover, π1(X) ∼ = Z, X ∼ =or (S1 × S3 )# b CP 2 , where the second is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism for the complex orientation of X.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.3
candidates.name: A sharpened Euler–signature inequality
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3 (A sharpened Euler–signature inequality).
candidates.statement: Let S be a connected closed smooth complex surface whose topological universal cover is contractible. Write χtop(S) for its Euler characteristic and σ(S) for its signature in the complex orientation. Then χtop(S) ≥ 9 5 |σ(S)|. If χtop(S) > 0, then S is of general type; otherwise χtop(S) = σ(S) = 0.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.1
candidates.name: Surface reductions
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.1 (Surface reductions).
candidates.statement: Let V be a minimal compact complex surface with b1(V ) = 1, κ(V ) = −∞, and b2(V ) > 0. (i) If V has a nonzero effective divisor C with C2 = 0, then V has a global spherical shell. (ii) If V has exactly b2(V ) rational curves, then V has a global spherical shell. Here the conclusion supplies an embedded open neighborhood of S3 ⊂ C2 \ {0} with connected complement in V .
candidates.cited_by: Our two surface-theoretic reductions are the following established results.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.1.
candidates.statement: For p = 0 or p = 2, every admissible pair (a, b) and every s ∈ Z, the complex (4.4) has closed ranges and finite-dimensional cohomology. Its cohomology agrees with that of the maximal weighted L2 complex and is represented by forms which belong to Wk a,b for every k. There are bounded homotopies of degree −1 which gain one derivative, modulo projections onto these harmonic spaces. For the periodic trivial datum the single-linear-weight complex with ρ ̸= 0 is acyclic, in every Sobolev realization. The operator bounds may depend on the fixed rates and the datum.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.6
candidates.name: Tail asymptotics
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.6 (Tail asymptotics).
candidates.statement: Let E satisfy (4.3). A finite-growth holomorphic section of KY ⊗ E or KY ⊗ E−1 on a positive tail vanishes on a shorter positive tail. A finite-growth holomorphic section of E has, in the prescribed trivialization at either end on which it is defined, the expansion s = c± + O(e−δ|h| ) for some δ > 0, with the same conclusion for every derivative of the error. On the positive end c+ = 0 implies s = 0. Consequently the positive-end coefficient is injective on global weighted holomorphic sections of E.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.8
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.8.
candidates.statement: Every compact line-bundle datum admits an integrable (0, 1)-connection sat- isfying (4.3) with any prescribed finite γ > 0. For every such structure and every admissible pair, H0,2 a,b (Y, E) = 0. (4.15) For every a, b > 0, global weighted holomorphic sections have the two constant end coefficients and the exponentially decaying errors described in Proposition 4.6; the map s 7→ c+ is injective.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.10
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.10.
candidates.statement: Let E be a compact datum supported in a cut-open period of a finite cyclic quotient Xn = Y/Tn, with its trivializations fixed in collars of the cut. Equip E with an integrable operator dE satisfying (4.3), and let e be its compact support Chern class. For a, b > 0 its weighted Dolbeault index is 2 ∑ q=0 (−1)q dim H0,q a,b (Y, E) = 1 + 1 2 ( e2 − KY · e ) . (4.16) The products on the right are compact support intersection pairings. In particular, if e2 = KY · e, the section space is one-dimensional, its positive-end coefficient is nonzero on every nonzero section, and H0,1 a,b (Y, E) = 0.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.11
candidates.name: A section with different end limits
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.11 (A section with different end limits).
candidates.statement: Let E be one of the data in Lemma 3.1, and write e2 = KY · e = −m with m > 0. Given any finite γ > 0, E admits a holomorphic structure whose Dolbeault operator, in its fixed end frames, differs from the trivial operator by O(e−γ|h|) in every derivative. Finally, an order-zero (2, 1)-current supported in {h ≤ C} whose masses on negative unit height slabs are at most C0eµl belongs to this complex whenever b > µ. candidates.statement: Let (X, F) be a smooth connected complex projective contact Fano manifold of dimension 2n + 1, with n ≥ 1, and let L = TX/F. candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3 (Projective contact manifolds).
candidates.statement: Let (X, F) be a smooth connected complex projective contact manifold of dimension 2n + 1, where n ≥ 1. Its second Betti number determines the following alternatives. 1. If b2(X) = 1, then (X, F) is contact-isomorphic to the adjoint variety Yg, with its canonical contact distribution, for a simple complex Lie algebra g. 2. If b2(X) ≥ 2, then there is a smooth connected complex projective manifold Z of dimension n + 1 and a biholomorphism X ≃ P(T∗ Z). Here P(T∗Z) parametrizes lines in cotangent spaces, equivalently hyperplanes in tangent spaces. This assertion identifies the underlying manifolds, without imposing compatibility with the given distribution F. Conversely, every adjoint variety of complex dimension 2n + 1 and every projectivized cotangent bundle in the second alternative admits a contact structure. Thus these are precisely the underlying manifolds of smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds in these dimensions.

candidates.statement: For each d > 0 and ϵ > 0, there is a positive integer n = n(d, ϵ) such that the following holds. Let X be an ϵ-lc rationally Gorenstein variety of dimension d, and let f : X → Z be a birational Fano type contraction with −KX nef over Z. For every closed z ∈ Z, there is an effective rational divisor ∆ over a neighbourhood of z such that (X, ∆) is klt there and n(KX + ∆) is Cartier and linearly trivial there, after shrinking the neighbourhood.

candidates.label: Corollary 3
candidates.name: Real boundaries
candidates.heading: Corollary 3 (Real boundaries).
candidates.statement: Over C, the conclusion of Theorem 1 holds for effective real boundaries B with KX + B real Cartier, with the same uniform dependence on d and ϵ.

candidates.label: Proposition A.5
candidates.name: Uniform charts
candidates.heading: Proposition A.5 (Uniform charts).
candidates.statement: At a chosen vertical place in Lemma A.4(ii), after a bounded degree extension of k(W) and a chosen extension of the DVR and of the place, there is a toroidal cone representing the place, with nonnegative coordinates (x, e∗), Mx = re∗. (A.2) Here M ranges over a finite list of integral matrices of bounded sizes, r is integral (possibly huge), e∗ is value of the new uniformizer, and original uniformizer value is ρe∗ with positive bounded ρ. Nonzero integral solutions on the cone give divisorial valuations (not necessarily primitive after restriction); evaluations of discrepancy data always refer to homogeneous values by restriction. For horizontal places as in the first bullet one just has an orthant on a bounded generic resolution, without e∗. For any effective generalized CY data A on X1 over S, values on these cones are finite continuous homogeneous piecewise linear, and are Lipschitz in x with uniform constant at fixed e∗ > 0 (uniform homogeneous Lipschitz in the horizontal case). Constants depend on the boundedness in this Mori step and the complement indices, not on r, vertical coefficients, or the nef part index or the chosen data A. In particular finitely many differences at fixed parameter separations have uniform Lipschitz bounds as well.

candidates.label: Corollary A.8
candidates.name: Horizontal variants
candidates.heading: Corollary A.8 (Horizontal variants).
candidates.statement: The chart and metric conclusions have the following two variants. (i) The same tailorable bounded complement and homogeneous chart argument works if we are working over an algebraically closed generic field, with the relevant effective CYs on a Q-factorial model of Fano type, and have boundedness only up to isomorphism in codimension one of these models. (ii) A Cartier rational b-order function N with effective trace of degree O(ξ) on the bounded model, b-linearly Q-equivalent to a difference of b-nef parts both of trace degrees O(ξ), has horizontal Lipschitz constant O(ξ), including when ξ → 0+.

candidates.statement: In Lemma C.3, let gi,1, . . . , gi,ri be any finite list contained in S(C1LiDi) for one fixed C1. For all sufficiently large i, the entire field Fi = k(gi,1, . . . , gi,ri ), and its relative algebraic closure inside k(Vi), lie in K∗,i. Thus every test from part (ii) is exactly zero on every nonzero element of these fields at that same index, without a degree-dependent eventual qualification. More generally, a valuation trivial on a subfield remains trivial on any algebraic extension of it inside its valued overfield.

candidates.statement: In the above setting the following statements hold. (i) The discrepancy of (X, H) at (P, y) is a(P), and its discrepancy at a pure weight is zero. Consequently D(P) = min y∈∆P (P, y)(h) = γ(P) + L(u)(P) (D.6) is the b-pullback of an effective ample rational divisor D on Vu. (iii) At every actual prime P of Vµ, a minimizer y of (D.5) can be chosen so that e(P, y) is a primitive prime order on X, for some positive integer e. For this choice, a(P) + (P, y)(h) = 1 e , ey ∈ Hom(M, Z). Each Vµ is of Fano type. At an actual prime outside the floor {a = 0}, the same minimizer satisfies a(P) = 1, e = 1, (P, y)(h) = 0. (D.8)

candidates.name: Pinning obstruction
candidates.heading: Theorem G.1 (Pinning obstruction).
candidates.statement: Fix an integer n > 0 and ϵ > 0. There is no sequence of the following data satisfying all the conditions below. candidates.heading: Proposition G.4 (High-scale pin).
candidates.statement: Consider a high stage with pre-pinning slice, working valuation w, baseline height B, scale L, and s selected values as above. The added tests are exact on that slice, all old tests and proportionalities remain in force, and the accumulated positive symbols remain algebraically independent at the exact minimizer and working valuation in (iii) below. (ii) The selected values either vanish or lie on a single rational line. In the line case their proportions have the bounds (G.3), with L− = L. An old anchor remains the anchor; if a new anchor is chosen, its scale is L1 = L. (iii) The baseline height is retained unless an anchor is first chosen, in which case it may change to the rational height (G.5). It satisfies (G.4) on the new actual slice. At its exact minimizer v′, and at an arbitrarily close rank refinement w′, the anchor, when present, satisfies |v′(Y + 0 )|, |w′(Y + 0 )| ≥ cL1. manuscripts.title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Every smooth connected complex projective Fano variety of dimension six with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Albanese fibres and uniformization
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Albanese fibres and uniformization).
candidates.statement: Let X be a connected compact Kähler manifold whose holomorphic tangent bundle is nef in the analytic sense. Suppose 0 ≤ d = dimC X − ̃ q(X) ≤ 6. Then there is a connected finite étale cover X′ → X with the following properties. 1. The Albanese map α : X′ → A = Alb(X′) is a smooth proper surjection with connected fibres, where A is a complex torus of dimension ̃ q(X). Every fibre is rational homogeneous of dimension d, with a point allowed when d = 0. 2. There is one such fibre F for which α is a holomorphically locally trivial F-bundle. The ordinary universal cover of X is biholomorphic to ̃ X ≃ F × C̃ q(X) . It is therefore biholomorphic to a quasi-projective variety and is holomorphically convex. Its Remmert reduction is the projection F × C̃ q(X) −→ C̃ q(X) . In particular, these conclusions hold whenever dimC X ≤ 6.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth complex Fano manifold of dimension n with nef tangent bundle, and let V be a component of rational curves of minimal anticanonical degree d. Then U and V are smooth projective varieties, dim V = n + d − 3, the map π : U → V is a smooth P1-fibration, and e : U → X is smooth and surjective with connected fibres of dimension d − 2. For every fibre C of π, Te|C ≃ OP1 (−1)⊕(d−2) . (2.3)

candidates.label: Proposition 2.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.2.
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth complex Fano sixfold with ρ(X) = 1 and nef tangent bundle. Then either X ≃ P6, X ≃ Q6, or its pseudoindex is 4 or 5.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.1.
candidates.statement: A smooth complex Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle, Picard number one and pseudoindex four is rational homogeneous.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.2.
candidates.statement: Every smooth complex Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle, Picard number one and pseudoindex five is isomorphic to Gr(2, 5).

candidates.label: Corollary 7.1
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.1.
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth connected complex projective Fano variety with nef tangent bundle and 1 ≤ dimC X ≤ 6. Then X admits a positive Kähler–Einstein metric. More precisely, with the Ricci-form convention ρ(ω) = −i∂ ¯ ∂ log det(gab̄), there is a Kähler form ω such that ρ(ω) = ω, [ω] = 2πc1(−KX).

candidates.statement: Let Z be a smooth connected projective complex variety of dimension d with H0(Z, Ωq Z) = 0 for every 1 ≤ q ≤ d. Let D ≥ 0 be an integral divisor. Suppose that J = −KZ + D has a semipositive singular Hermitian metric hJ satisfying Z Z |sD|2 hJ < ∞. If a line bundle L on Z has a semipositive singular Hermitian metric with locally bounded weights, then there exist integers a > 0 and b ≥ 0 such that H0 (Z, aL + bD) ̸= 0.

candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Finite cover with compact torus monodromy).
candidates.statement: Let X be a smooth connected pro- jective complex variety whose anticanonical bundle has a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive Chern curvature. There are a connected finite étale cover ν : S → X, an integer a ≥ 0, and smooth connected projective varieties F and Z with the following properties. 1. For a suitable Kähler metric on X, the common universal cover of X and S has a holomorphic isometric decomposition e X = Ca × F × Z. (2.1) The compact factors are simply connected. The induced metric on F is Ricci-flat, and KF has a nowhere-zero parallel holomorphic section. The anticanonical bundle of Z is smoothly semipositive, and H0 (Z, Ωp Z) = 0 (p > 0), Hq (Z, OZ) = 0 (q > 0). (2.2) The variety Z is rationally connected when it has positive dimension. 2. Suppose conversely that, on an extensive graph, disjoint indexed-block assignments to planks of common widths a, b have masses at least T(κ, a, b) in exponent. Set a = logN a, u = logN (K/b), χ = a + u. (4.3) If χ < 1, the isotropic scale cut described below gives an ensemble at resolution N′ = Nb/(Ka) = N1−χ with matching sharp upper and lower bounds. candidates.name: Canonical equality profile
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.4 (Canonical equality profile).
candidates.statement: There is an exact equality whose profile is F(κ) = β(κ − τ)+, 0 < τ < 1, ℓ = 1 − τ, β = v/ℓ ≤ 1. (5.11) Its deficit is v, and τ is the least initial delay among all equalities with deficit v.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Stationary data
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Stationary data).
candidates.statement: There is a realizing sequence of canonical equalities and compatible packet assignments for which the preceding collapsed law, event labels, and matrix forms have the following properties. All local upper bounds and original index weights are retained. (i) Along an index, occupied time blocks have regular branching exponent s0 = 1 − β ≥ 0. More precisely, for fixed c < b ≤ 1, an occupied Ic contains Nℓ(1−β)(b−c)+o(1) (5.20) occupied Ib blocks. The event normals on that index in Ic lie in a range of size ΘcNo(1). (ii) For 0 < c ≤ 1 there are assigned packets Bc on the occupied Ic blocks, with raw active index mass at least nc = ∆hN(B∗+τ)c+dw(1−c) (5.21) in exponent. On each fixed time block the assigned index sets are disjoint, and each retained index has one packet owner there. The used normals of a packet differ from its spatial normal by at most ΘcNo(1). (iii) In every used event frame, the widths of Bc in the four forms (5.18) are bounded by LX(c), LY (c), LU (c), LV (c) up to subpower expansion. Equivalently, their negative log exponents are ρ + wc, ρ + (w − τ)c, ρ + (w − ℓ)c, ρ + (w − 1)c, (5.22) 47 (iv) The data and packet lower bounds coexist on any prescribed finite list of scales and tests, and hence on countable lists by slow diagonals. They persist, in exponent, on typical nondeficient parts after extensive regular refinements. All packet memberships are memberships of original active indices on their physical intervals. In a chart registered at Ic, the packet at a finer Ib is determined by the index, chart, and Ib; a matrix cell in that chart is determined by the index and chart.

manuscripts.title: Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let K ⊂ R4. Suppose that for every e ∈ S3 there is a point ae ∈ R4 such that {ae + te : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} ⊂ K. Then dimH K = 4.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.16
candidates.name: Initial horizon bound
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.16 (Initial horizon bound).
candidates.statement: Every homogeneous exact problem satisfies H(E) ≤ L.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.17
candidates.name: Reduction to a bad weighted problem
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.17 (Reduction to a bad weighted problem).
candidates.statement: If a set K ⊂ R4, with no measurability or compactness assumption, contains a unit segment in every direction and satisfies dimH K < 4, then there are 0 < d < 1, S, η > 0, and a tempered homogeneous exact problem E of version 2 in C(d) such that H(E) > 0.

candidates.label: Corollary 3.4
candidates.name: Local matching of scalar graphs
candidates.heading: Corollary 3.4 (Local matching of scalar graphs).
candidates.statement: Fix the base dimension, algebraic degrees, real comparison balls with fixed holomorphic margins, and d0 < 1. There is ε∗ > 0 with the following property. Let M, ∆ > 0, and put R = M/∆. For sufficiently large R, two lists of real-on-real algebraic sheets cannot satisfy all of the following, with 0 < ε ≤ ε∗ and d ≤ d0: 1. each list has at most Rd+ε members, and each member is within MRε in norm of one common algebraic reference sheet; 2. a subprobability law on pairs of indices and a common real base point in the comparison domain has total mass at least R−ε, with each index-base marginal bounded by Rεπκ,i dz, where the πκ,i are probability weights, separately in each color; 3. on its events, the two values differ by at most ∆Rε, whereas the norm of their difference on the comparison ball is at least MR−ε. Fixed multiplicative constants may be absorbed by decreasing ε∗ or taking R larger.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Critical paths
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Critical paths).
candidates.statement: Fix the model version and its parameters j, S, η, and suppose bad problems exist. With d∗, k, ℓ as above, the following conclusions hold. 1. Every maximizing sequence of length-one exact problems satisfies sup 0≤r≤1 fi(r) − fi(0) − d∗r −→ 0. (4.5) Only the relative profiles occur; no bound on fi(0) is required. 2. For every fixed finite ordered grid of target depths ending at one, there are nested true systems at actual depths tending to those targets. Their cumulative horizons tend to kr, and their segment horizons, in their own length units, tend to k. Both the coarsened and remaining problems used at each step are maximizing after their individual length normalizations. Full layer assignments, priors and incidence witnesses can be retained in addition to the final path incidences. 3. In version 2 with ℓ < ∞, for every ζ > 0 one may choose the base maximizing sequence and these paths so that cumulative narrowness at a target r, and narrowness increments between targets, equal the corresponding linear values with slope ℓ, up to O(ζ)+oi(1). The base sequence has terminal optimal narrowness supremum at most ℓ + ζ. 4. If ℓ = ∞, every newly obtained maximizing sequence admits, on subsequences, true terminal systems with relative horizons tending to k and relative narrowness tending to infinity. Thus arbitrarily large narrowness increments can be required on each of finitely many successive positive-length segments.

candidates.label: Corollary 4.4
candidates.name: Depth-zero normalization and vanishing-depth nodes
candidates.heading: Corollary 4.4 (Depth-zero normalization and vanishing-depth nodes).
candidates.statement: A sequence of depth-zero, horizon-zero known normalizations of a maximizing sequence is again maximizing, provided the 50 normalizations have the actual subpower success and terminal knowledge required in Lemma 2.13. This assertion does not require bounded absolute density exponents. On any maximizing sequence one may choose true nodes at positive depths bi → 0 whose horizon exponents tend to zero, retaining the relative-profile estimates at those nodes in the slowly diagonalized sense.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.7
candidates.name: Prepared tangent data
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.7 (Prepared tangent data).
candidates.statement: Assume ℓ < ∞, and use the guarded diagonal constructed above. One can retain all but o(1) of the relative mass of the original final path and choose an interior parent window with the following properties. Write d = d∗, N = Nϵn 0 , and use K = No(1) for analytical estimates. There is one prepared path probability µprep = P A pAλ0 A, where pA = µprep{A} and λ0 A is its conditional probability in parent A. On the retained parents, λ0 A ≤ KνA × dt, where νA is the prior conditioned on the full parent trajectory assignment and dt is uniform parent time. Subsequent omissions restrict this mixture and leave its reference weights and probabilities fixed. 53 1. At every required bounded tangent depth s, the true label Qs has thickness as = N−s, time length qs ∼log,N N−ks, and spatial determinant Js ∼log,N qj sN−ℓs in version 2; omit the last factor in version 1. Its largest width is comparable to qs in logarithmic order, and its full assigned trajectory mass satisfies νQ ∼log,N ad sJs. 2. For the restricted incidence laws, pure hidden and native-signal bins of width p have the instantaneous joint base-density ceiling Kpd on the required finite grids. In unit coordinates of a Qs-box, the base marginal has density at most KqsνQ, with masses still measured in parent time. 3. Let v = V in version 1 and in the case ℓ = 0. For 0 < ℓ < ∞, let Z, Y be the major and minor parent coordinates and put v = Z′. The fixed conditional parent palette πA, the velocity marginal of λ0 A, satisfies πA(Bp) ≤ KpS. If E denotes the end history, then before likelihood deletion the required velocity bin satisfies X A pAIλ0 A ([v]; E) = o(log N). Thus the information bound is averaged with the fixed parent weights. 4. Required finite-mesh point states and path labels have lists at the original pL bounded by fixed powers of actual path factors and logarithms. Sufficiently deep histories leave only K options for these point states. Each fitted test has at most K local graph choices approximating w to Kas on retained incidences in their cores. After composition with the native test, their fixed-order derivatives are bounded by K on the used normalized interiors. These graph bounds and capped full-layer incidence witnesses can be prepared before arbitrary later inverse-subpower selections. When 0 < ℓ < ∞, major-coordinate fullness and the coefficients of the tilted-box rows can be prepared with actual N0-subpower bounds. The joint and conditional consequences of these fixed laws are stated in Lemma 4.8 below.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.11
candidates.name: Conversion of candidates to actual improvements
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.11 (Conversion of candidates to actual improvements).
candidates.statement: Consider the guarded tangent diagonal of Proposition 4.7. Suppose that, on a further subsequence of every subsequence carrying any substantial residual of the reference path, that residual supplies a time-improvement or strip candidate in the sense of Definition 4.10. Its depth remains in a bounded tangent range and its gain has a fixed positive finite limit, or is a fixed positive number. Then one of the original-resolution outputs excluded by Lemma 4.6 exists. Its original success is at least ppath/ log N0, and its lists and geometric slacks are bounded by a fixed scenario-dependent power of Kpath log N0. Its complete original-coordinate complexity, including list tables, is bounded by a polynomial in Mpath depending only on that fixed scenario. Consequently the candidate hypothesis is impossible on this diagonal.

candidates.label: Corollary 4.13
candidates.name: Breadth before sparse selections
candidates.heading: Corollary 4.13 (Breadth before sparse selections).
candidates.statement: In version 2 with ℓ = 0, let a substantial path residual carry a measurable discrete state, including its tangent parent. Suppose the state is known on these events at the original pL with list size bounded by a fixed power of actual path factors and logarithms, and has at most K possible values given the used deep end histories. For every fixed κ, u > 0, the total residual probability of states whose conditional velocity law puts mass at least κ within distance N−u of an affine line tends to zero. In version 1 the corresponding assertion for intervals follows from the angular cap. These statements can be prepared at reciprocal-subpower separation thresholds before arbitrary sparse selections. They persist under selections of whole conditioning states, or controlled fixed-fraction selections within them; no version-2 breadth assertion is made for every velocity-dependent inverse- subpower subfamily.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.4
candidates.name: Scalar-normal first jet
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.4 (Scalar-normal first jet).
candidates.statement: Assume Definition 5.2. Fix a finite nested hierarchy of dyadic time lengths of fixed positive power, with finest length H∗. If the available floor is sufficiently fine—ζ ≤ H3 ∗ /K suffices after enlarging K—then a dense restriction of the single-time labels admits a time-only row A(t), bounded by K, such that |F(v) − F(u) − (v − u)A(u)| ≤ KH11/10 (5.15) whenever the retained active times u, v lie in the same designated interval of length H. Put J1(l, t) = x′ l(t) − F(t)y′ l − A(t)yl(t). For every finite presampled tuple and every dense tested event as in Lemma 5.3, on which all tested times carry the retained labels, H(J1(l, t)r | T, Sl(t)r) = o∗ if r ≥ H (1−d)/64 ∗ (5.16) at the available resolutions. The row A and the single-time restriction are fixed before the tuple and the later event are chosen.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.5
candidates.name: Planar dot-product alternative
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.5 (Planar dot-product alternative).
candidates.statement: For every ε > 0 there are η, δ0 > 0 such that the following holds for 0 < p ≤ δ0. Let A, B ⊂ [0, 1]2, and suppose that Ns(E ∩ B(z, w)) ≤ p−η w/s for E ∈ {A, B}, p ≤ s ≤ w. (5.17) At least one of the following alternatives holds: 1. There are affine lines ℓ, ℓ⊥ with perpendicular directions such that both Np(A ∩ {z : dist(z, ℓ) ≤ p}), Np(B ∩ {z : dist(z, ℓ⊥ ) ≤ p}) are at least pε−1. 2. Every restricted triple set H ⊂ A × B × B with Np(H) ≥ pη−3 admits a scale s ≥ p and an interval J, |J| ≥ p−ηs, for which Ns J ∩ {a · (b − b′ ) : (a, b, b′ ) ∈ H}  ≥ (|J|/s)1−ε .

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: Higher-jet polynomial fitting
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Higher-jet polynomial fitting).
candidates.statement: For the parameters M, d, h and hierarchy just defined, assume Definition 5.2, including the parameter-bin cap, and the floor condition Equa- tion (5.28). Then a dense set of labeled incidences (l, t) has the following property. There is a row-valued polynomial P of degree at most M, with coefficients bounded by K, such that in the h-block containing t, |F(v) − P(v)| ≤ KhM+1/4 on labeled times v ∈ El of length at least h/K, including v = t. The polynomial may depend on the incidence. The conclusion applies anew to any dense restriction of the input labels with the same upper hypotheses.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: Isotropic improvement
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (Isotropic improvement).
candidates.statement: Consider the tangent data of Proposition 4.7, with 0 < k ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ d < 1, either in version 1, where j = 1, or in version 2 with j = 2 and optimized narrowness ℓ = 0. In every substantial residual of the reference path one can, after passing to a subsequence, find a packet Q = Qs, of thickness a = N−s and time length h ∼log,N ak, and a time-improvement candidate of thickness a2 = ahe2 , e2 > 0. The candidate has incidence mass at least hνQ K  a2 a d , K = No(1) . Writing the candidate as Pnew, its bounds |Pnew| ≤ Ka2 and |∂wPnew| ≤ K hold on its assigned trajectories throughout the same h-length block. The hidden derivative is bounded below by K−1 on the counted incidences, and its hidden curvature is at most K/a2. In version 1 the test has the special form w − F(t, y), with F quadratic. In version 2 it is a quadratic in (t, y, w).

candidates.name: Physical velocity graph

candidates.statement: For a sufficiently fine fixed power b, there is a row G = (G0, Gy), constant on each Wb and bounded by K, such that on a substantial reference family |X′ (t) − G(Wb) · v| ≤ bκ , (6.11) where κ > 0 depends only on m and 1 − d. candidates.statement: There are a subpower Kqual = No(1) and sets UN of graph-reference incidences such that eN := Λref(UN ) Lref −→ 0. (6.13) Every reference incidence outside UN admits a row-valued polynomial in t, of degree at most M and coefficients bounded by Kqual, which approximates G within hM on reference-labeled times of its indexed trajectory of ordinary duration at least h/Kqual in the same Qs-block, including that incidence.

candidates.name: Zero horizon in the scalar model
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.9 (Zero horizon in the scalar model).
candidates.statement: For every fixed admissible choice of angular parameters and every d < 1, a version 1 exact problem in C(d) has H(E) = 0. In particular there is no bad problem in version 1.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.6
candidates.name: Retained-edge planar rigidity
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.6 (Retained-edge planar rigidity).
candidates.statement: Under Assumption 7.2, after increasing to a new subpower K∗, there are a represented κ0, at least h−2/K∗ original edges of Gκ0 , and |λ|+|cA|+|cB| ≤ K∗ such that on those edges |x2 − λx1 − cA| + |y2 − λy1 − cB| ≤ K∗h. candidates.label: Theorem 8.2
candidates.name: Scalar mesh projection
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.2 (Scalar mesh projection).
candidates.statement: Let ν be a probability law on trajectories (t, y(t), x(t)), where y is scalar affine, x is scalar quadratic, and all coefficients are bounded by K = No(1). Additional trajectory coordinates are permitted. Let µact ≤ Kν ⊗ dt have mass at least 1/K. Fix a = N−s, s > 0, and a dyadic mesh σ ∼log,N N−M in (t, y), with fixed M > s. Suppose c > 0 and its reciprocal are polynomially bounded and, for some d < 1, • each (t, y)-mesh cell and x-bin of width p = N−r, 0 ≤ r ≤ s, have active mass at most Kσ2cpd; • the number of occupied (σ, σ, a)-cells, multiplied by σ2, is at most Kc−1a−d. The depth hypotheses use fixed powers, with the rounding and interpolation conventions of Section 2. They imply d ≥ 0: otherwise summing the unit-width cap over terminal support contradicts the dense total mass. After a dense restriction and passage to a subsequence, there are labels with disjoint trajectory assignments and a common scale σ/K ≤ β ≤ K, up to subpower factors, such that each label has • a moving affine interval of width Kβ containing its assigned y-trajectories throughout unit time; • a quadratic F(t, y) with |x − F(t, y)| ≤ Ka throughout unit time on its assigned trajectories; • assigned active mass at least cadβ/K. The quadratic norm is at most K in coordinates adapted to the moving interval of scale β. If, at r = s, appending a y′-bin of width N−u gives the mass ceiling a further factor KN−S1u for 0 < u ≤ u1, with fixed S1, u1 > 0, then β ∼log,N 1.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.4
candidates.name: Wide-interval improvement
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.4 (Wide-interval improvement).
candidates.statement: Use the finite-narrowness parent data of Section 8.2: the joint caps, conditional palette domination at fine point and path states, and the true Qs graph lists. The observable X may be the native signal or any other bounded quadratic-along-lines signal with these data. At scales s, s + u, s + c2, put a = as, a1 = aN−u , a2 = aN−c2 . Suppose that simultaneous projected labels Φ, Φ1, Φ2 of the type constructed above, including their mass bounds, occur on dense mass and use the same α’s. Let βmin, βmax be their smallest and largest interval scales. Assume 0 < c2 < (1 − d)u/4 and βmax ≤ Kgs, bs/βmin + hsβmax/βmin ≤ N−(Cd+3)u , Cd = 10/(1 − d), up to subpower factors, with common scale exponents. Take all comparison meshes, including the intercept mesh χ, sufficiently fine in fixed powers relative to these widths and hs, bs, a1, so the transverse evaluation errors are negligible even at width a1. Then some true Q = Qs admits a quadratic predictor in the full base (t, Z, Y ) for X, of error Ka2 throughout its block on assigned trajectories, carrying original active mass at least qsνQ(a2/a)d /K. Here νQ is the full trajectory assignment weight.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.5
candidates.name: Reduction to the horizontal model
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.5 (Reduction to the horizontal model).
candidates.statement: Suppose βs = N−B0+o(1) with ℓs < B0 ≤ ℓs+M. On every substantial residual either there is a strip-improvement candidate, or a true-parent normalization gives k = ℓ and Equation (8.1), with fixed e0 > 0. At sufficiently small prescribed relative depths the whole true boxes have horizontal scale H and transverse scale H2 in Equation (8.2). Mass is normalized by the chosen parent’s full assignment times its time length.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.2
candidates.name: Critical-rate improvement
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.2 (Critical-rate improvement).
candidates.statement: If 2k = 1, every substantial residual of the prepared horizontal problem yields a time-improvement candidate in the sense of Proposition 4.11. More precisely, for a sufficiently small fixed s > 0 and any fixed 0 < c < ks/2, one can choose a true Qs and an affine base predictor whose hidden-variable test has width Karas+c, hidden derivative one, and counted mass at least K−1 qrν(Qr)mQs N−dc in the initial tangent parent. Its fit holds throughout the selected block on the assigned trajectories.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.5

candidates.heading: Proposition 9.5 (Parameter bootstrap below the critical rate).
candidates.statement: If 2k < 1, there is a fixed smax > 0 for which G(2k) holds. It can be applied anew to any dense input sequence and any subsequence. Any prescribed finite set of depths below smax can be used simultaneously on a further dense restriction, with current individual floors, unchanged earlier full-domain witnesses, and the original true assignment priors.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.6
candidates.name: Return to wide intervals
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.6 (Return to wide intervals).
candidates.statement: If 2k ̸= 1, every substantial residual of the horizontal problem supplies the hypotheses of Proposition 8.4 at three fixed nearby depths. Consequently it yields a time-improvement candidate with a fixed positive depth gain, full block fit, hidden derivative one, and the required original true-descendant mass. The assertion holds both for 2k < 1 and for 2k > 1.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.1
candidates.name: Exclusion of unbounded optimized narrowness
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.1 (Exclusion of unbounded optimized narrowness).
candidates.statement: In the second model’s extremal setup of Proposition 4.3, the global optimized narrowness ℓ is finite.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.2

candidates.heading: Proposition 10.2 (Full-time localization).
candidates.statement: In the setting of Equations (10.2) and (10.3), a permitted further selection admits full-time charts C with tangential width one and normal width gC = g2N2u 0 . (10.7) Their labels are known by the original p1 with actual subpower lists. The native test remains P∗. If nC and yC(t) are the normal and affine center of C, then every retained Q1-incidence satisfies, after a consistent choice of signs, |n1 − nC| ≤ K0g1, |nC · (y′ 1 − y′ C)| ≤ K0g1. (10.8) All assignments, geometric tests and coordinate changes have tempered bounds within each fixed Ei.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.1

candidates.statement: There is an absolute constant C0 such that, for every integer m ≥ 3, there is a map gm : {0, 1}m → ℓ1 satisfying ED(u, v) ≤ ∥gm(u) − gm(v)∥1 ≤ Dm ED(u, v), Dm = exp C0 p log m log log m  . (5.1) Here ED permits unit-cost substitutions as well as insertions and deletions.

candidates.heading: Proposition 5.2 (Uniform alphabet bound).
candidates.statement: There is an absolute constant C such that, for every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2, EΣ(d) ≤ exp C p log d log log d  (d ≥ 3). (5.2) Moreover, EΣ(1) = 1 and 1 ≤ EΣ(2) ≤ 2.

manuscripts.title: Finite-Circle Obstructions, Binary Codes, and Histogram Embeddings for Edit Distance

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There are absolute constants c, C > 0 and an integer d0 such that, for every integer d ≥ d0 and every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2, exp (︁ c √︁ log d log log d )︁ ≤ EΣ(d) ≤ exp (︁ C √︁ log d log log d )︁ . (1) Each of our two lower constructions supplies a binary subset whose words have one common length at most d and whose least ℓ1 distortion satisfies the lower bound. The upper bound is realized by a deterministic finite-dimensional map.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.1
candidates.name: Two binary substitutions
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1 (Two binary substitutions).
candidates.statement: Let A be a finite alphabet with A ≥ 2 letters. Each of the two constructions below gives an integer width w ≥ 1 with w = O(log(2A)), an absolute constant a > 0, and a map c : A → {0, 1}w such that, simultaneously for every integer L ≥ 0 and all x, y ∈ AL, awrL(x, y) ≤ rwL(c(x), c(y)) ≤ wrL(x, y). (23) Here c extends to words by concatenation. For arbitrary finite words, ED(c(x), c(y)) ≤ w ED(x, y). (24) The code and its width depend only on A, not on L.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.1
candidates.name: Uniform upper bound
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.1 (Uniform upper bound).
candidates.statement: There are absolute constants C > 0 and d0 ≥ 3 such that, for every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2 and every integer d ≥ d0, there are an integer M ≥ 1 and a deterministic map F : Σ≤d −→ ℓM 1 satisfying ED(x, y) ≤ ∥F(x) − F(y)∥1 ≤ exp (︁ C √︁ log d log log d )︁ ED(x, y) (x, y ∈ Σ≤d ). Here ℓM 1 is real, and both C and d0 are independent of Σ.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.1
candidates.name: Uniform upper embedding, companion theorem
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.1 (Uniform upper embedding, companion theorem).
candidates.statement: There are absolute constants C > 0 and d0 ≥ 3 such that, for every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2 and every integer d ≥ d0, there are an integer M ≥ 1 and one deterministic map f : Σ≤d → ℓM 1 satisfying ED(x, y) ≤ ∥f(x) − f(y)∥1 ≤ exp (︂ C √︁ log d log log d )︂ ED(x, y) (x, y ∈ Σ≤d ). Here ℓM 1 is RM with its usual ℓ1 norm. The domain includes the empty word, and ED is ordinary unit-cost insertion, deletion and substitution distance. The dimension may depend on Σ, d; the constants and threshold do not.
